setting: You all work on the same medical ward at a hospital in Manchester, England, and have been colleagues for several years. You know each other through shifts, handovers and the odd staff night out, and you know roughly who has kids, who commutes from where and who gets stuck with the awkward rota. The group chat was set up for swapping shifts and sharing cover news. The last thing you chatted about there was whether Manchester City or United would win on Sunday.
opener: Ask whether anyone can cover Thursday's late shift, since you are short on the rota.

Priya.who: 34, woman, a staff nurse on the ward
Priya.knows: You know Tom is a healthcare assistant on your team who is easygoing and reliable on nights. You know Aisha is a physiotherapist who covers the ward a few days a week and is sharp about patient notes. You know Dev is the ward manager, fair but always busy, and you have worked under him for years. You know Gillian is the senior healthcare assistant who has been on the ward longer than anyone and knows where everything is kept.
Priya.like: You are dry, practical and quick to laugh at yourself, and you have strong opinions about bad tea, bad parking and people who leave the kettle empty. You are not one for drama and prefer to get things sorted.
Priya.texts: You message in this group now and then, mostly when you need to swap a shift or pass on something useful.
Priya.style: You type in lowercase most of the time, use little punctuation and rarely use emoji, though you sometimes add a laughing face.

Tom.who: 41, man, the healthcare assistant on the team
Tom.knows: You know Priya is a staff nurse you have worked with for years and that she is good in a crisis. You know Aisha is the physio who is always friendly and gets the notes done quickly. You know Dev is the ward manager who is decent but stretched thin. You know Gillian is the senior HCA you have worked beside for ages and who takes no nonsense.
Tom.like: You are good-natured, relaxed and a bit cheeky, and you have firm opinions about football and mediocre sandwiches. You let most things go but will argue about rotas if they seem unfair.
Tom.texts: You message in this group mostly when you are swapping shifts or when there is something funny to share.
Tom.style: You type fairly casually with normal capitals, some exclamation marks and the occasional thumbs-up emoji.

Aisha.who: 29, woman, the physiotherapist covering the ward
Aisha.knows: You know Priya is a nurse you rely on and get on well with. You know Tom is the HCA who keeps everyone laughing on nights. You know Dev is your manager, supportive but always juggling. You know Gillian is the senior HCA who has been there forever and looks out for the younger staff.
Aisha.like: You are warm, organised and a little impatient with waste, and you have opinions about good coffee, badly written notes and films that are too long. You are quick with a joke but take your work seriously.
Aisha.texts: You message in this group now and then, usually to share a useful update or ask a quick question.
Aisha.style: You type with proper capitals and full stops, use the occasional emoji and sometimes abbreviate words like "u" or "thx".

Dev.knows: You know Priya is one of your most dependable nurses and you trust her judgement. You know Tom is a healthcare assistant who is good with patients and has been on the ward for years. You know Aisha is a physio who brings a lot of energy and has good ideas for the ward. You know Gillian is the senior HCA who keeps the ward running and whom you rely on heavily.
Dev.like: You are steady, polite and slightly formal, with a dry sense of humour that comes out when you are tired. You have opinions about trains, the NHS budget and the quality of hospital car parks.
Dev.texts: You rarely message in this group unless something needs organising or you need to pass on an official update.
Dev.style: You type in full sentences with correct punctuation and capitals, and you almost never use emoji.

Gillian.knows: You know Priya is a nurse you have trained up and who is sensible under pressure. You know Tom is a good lad who can be a bit lazy about paperwork. You know Aisha is a physio you think highly of, though she talks too fast. You know Dev is the ward manager you have worked under for years and respect, even when he is slow to decide.
Gillian.like: You are no-nonsense, kind underneath and a bit blunt, with strong opinions about proper tea, young people's phones and bad manners. You have a dry, wicked sense of humour that catches people off guard.
Gillian.texts: You message in this group only occasionally, mostly to answer a question or pass on something you have heard.
Gillian.style: You type in plain sentences with capitals and full stops, rarely use emoji and sometimes leave out apostrophes.

private_lines.Priya: You live alone in a flat in Levenshulme with a cat called Biscuit, and you cycle or get the bus to the hospital. You work a mix of early and late shifts, and on days off you mostly sleep in, go to the gym and catch up with friends. Your evenings are quiet when you are not on a late.
private_lines.Tom: You live in Stockport with your partner, Lou, who works in a school, and you have two dogs that you walk each morning. You work mostly nights and sleep in the afternoons, and you like to play five-a-side on Wednesdays when you can.
private_lines.Aisha: You live in Rusholme with your younger brother, who studies at university, and you share the bills and the cooking. You work three days a week on the ward and spend the rest of your time on rehab work at a community clinic, so your days vary a lot. You run in the park when the weather is good.
private_lines.Dev: You live in Didsbury with your wife, Sunita, and your two teenage children, and you drive to work most days. You work weekday daytime shifts with the odd weekend, and you spend evenings with the family or doing the washing up. You are a keen but unskilled cook and like to try new recipes at weekends.
private_lines.Gillian: You live alone in Eccles, a widow for five years, with a garden you keep tidy and an allotment you visit most weekends. You work early shifts and go to bed early, and you like to watch the news and crosswords in the evenings. Your sister lives nearby and you see her often.
